channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Tyler Warren caught 4-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
item.description: Warren wasn’t targeted in the first half as the team struggled to move the football consistently, catching his first ball on the team’s second possession of the third quarter. The Colts limp toward Tuesday’s trade deadline with numerous key players the subject of trade speculation, of which quarterback Daniel Jones, wide receiver Josh Downs, and running back Jonathan Taylor are amongst. Which is to say, Warren’s fantasy expectations could be heavily influenced by the team’s actions in the coming days, potentially setting the second-year tight end up to be the team’s top option during the second half of the season. Warren would appear to be in a solid spot on paper against the Dolphins in Week 10, where his fantasy value will be dependent on who remains with the team through Tuesday.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Braelon Allen had eight rushes for 23 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs, adding two catches for 21 yards.
item.description: Breece Hall, returning from his quad injury, led the New York backfield with 15 carries while adding three grabs out of the backfield. It was Allen, however, who led the Jets backfield in pass routes, 21 to 10. That sort of pass game usage could keep Allen viable in deeper formats since the Jets are going to be chasing points more weeks than not. Both Jets running backs average 4.1 yards per carry against an elite KC front seven. Allen plays the Bills in Week 10.-Denny Carter

item.title: Stefon Diggs caught 3-of-5 targets for 51 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams.
item.description: With the Commanders down three receivers, Diggs appeared prime for a decent day against a Rams secondary that was down two corners. Instead, the 32-year-old receiver was outshone by journeyman Van Jefferson for most of the day until the final drive of the game. With the Commanders looking to mount a game-tying drive, Diggs broke free into the secondary to make a 42-yard reception, which accounted for nearly all of his receiving production. In two games without Terry McLaurin, Diggs has averaged just 5.5 targets per game and totaled 89 yards and a touchdown. He’s far from the target hog he was in his prime, and shouldn’t be treated as anything more than a WR3/WR4 on Thursday night against the Giants.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Seth McGowan rushed six times for 45 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, losing three yards on one reception.
item.description: McGowan came on in relief of Jonathan Taylor on third-and-goal from the two late in the first quarter, cashing in on the opportunity for his first touchdown this season. a 36-yard scamper in the fourth quarter pushed his yards per carry mark to a healthy 7.5, dwarfing the 3.5 of Taylor. McGowan should not be on waiver wires ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, with the looming possibility that Taylor has played his final snap for the Colts.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Antonio Williams caught 3-of-6 targets for 25 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams.
Bo Nix completed 25-of-37 passes for 237 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in the Broncos’ 26-21, Week 9 win over the Panthers.
item.description: Today was only Nix’s third multi-score start of the season through the air, though it was also his second in as many weeks. It came as No. 1 wideout Jaylen Waddle left with a first half concussion. Nix’s were a three-yard precision dart to Courtland Sutton and 31-yard busted coverage strike to a returning Pat Bryant. He also extended a few key plays with his scrambling ability, most notably avoiding a massive third down sack on the Broncos’ opening drive. It was not a perfect day, but Nix has inarguably been playing better since his dismal Thursday Night Football outing three weeks ago. Now he must wait and see on Waddle’s Week 11 status against the Raiders’ awful defense, but Bryant’s healthy return could be a massive development. Nix will be a solid QB2 streamer next Sunday.-Patrick Daugherty

item.title: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 28 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams, adding two receptions for 41 additional yards.
Jonathan Taylor rushed 13 times for 46 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, adding 18 yards on five receptions.
item.description: Taylor also lost a key fumble in the fourth quarter following the team’s second takeaway of the game, leaving fantasy managers wanting more in what could have been his final game in Indianapolis. Taylor has been the subject of significant trade speculation and rumor as we head toward Tuesday’s trade deadline, although teams will need to take on his recently-signed contract extension that ties him to the Colts through the 2028 season. Things started off rough as Taylor was subbed out on third-and-goal from the two, watching from the sideline as Seth McGowan punched it in for the team’s only rushing score of the game. It did not get better from their for Taylor’s fantasy managers as the Colts played through consistently negative game script, limiting his volume in the process. Taylor’s next opponent remains uncertain, although he currently lines up to take on the reeling Dolphins in Week 10, at least as long as he remains with the Colts.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Kyren Williams rushed 15 times for 45 yards in the Rams’ Week 9 win over the Commanders, adding three receptions for 16 additional yards.
Bryce Young completed 28-of-39 passes for 276 yards, three touchdowns and an interception in the Panthers’ 26-21, Week 9 loss to the Broncos, also losing a fumble.
item.description: Young’s three-score start was his first since Week 2, though the two turnovers really put a damper on things. Young’s fourth quarter fumble short-circuited a potential game-winning drive, while his interception came in the end zone. Now, it was one of the more unlucky plays we have ever seen in the NFL — a ball seemingly everyone thought bounced off the ground actually bounced off a player into Devon Key’s arms — but Young put too much on the negative side of the ledger for the Panthers to pull this one out. They’ve now lost three straight games to fall to 3-5 on the season. Young at least snapped a streak of three straight starts with a sub-60 completion percentage. He also converted a late 4th-and-18 with an amazing throw. Young remains a frustrating option on the QB1/2 borderline heading into a golden Week 10 matchup with the Saints.-Patrick Daugherty
